title: How to Ask Someone Out: Example Messages for Every Situation — cv.cm
description: How to ask someone out without pressure: specific plans, example messages for chat, school, work and friends, what to do with "maybe", and first-meeting safety.
h1: How do you ask someone out?
answer: Ask for something small and specific: a day, a place and about an hour, such as "Want to get coffee on Saturday afternoon?" Say it plainly so they know it is a date, and give an easy way out. If they say yes, confirm details. If they say "maybe" or are busy without offering another time, ask once more at most, then let them come to you.

sections.h: The simple rule: specific, small and easy to answer
body: Most invitations fail not because of the person asking, but because the question is vague. "We should hang out sometime" is easy to agree with and never act on. "Do you want to try the new noodle place on Thursday after class?" gives a clear yes or no.

A good first invitation is small: coffee, a walk, a snack, an exhibition, an hour or two. Small plans are easier to say yes to and easier to leave if it does not feel right. A long dinner or a day trip can come later.

Many people stop themselves because they expect a no. Research by Francis Flynn and Vanessa Lake on direct requests found that people tend to underestimate how often others will say yes when asked directly. Their studies were about asking for help, not dates, but the lesson carries over: a clear, polite question gets more yes answers than people fear, and a no is usually a kind one.

body: In Japan, people often search for デート誘い方 (how to invite someone on a date). The same idea works there and everywhere: a gentle, concrete plan, and a way for them to say no without losing face, such as "if you're free" or "no pressure".

ul: After a good conversation or a fun moment, not after a bad day.
When you have shared some interest back and forth, not on the first message with someone you just matched.
In private or by message, not in front of a group, where saying no would be embarrassing.
Not at a time of stress for them: right before exams, a big deadline, or a family emergency.
With a few days' notice for a weekend plan. Last-minute plans are fine once you know each other better.

body: If you are not sure whether they are interested, a small invitation is often the clearest way to find out. Their answer tells you more than weeks of reading signs. If you want to review what you have seen first, cv.cm's crush test can help you think it through.

body.note: The one-reschedule rule: if they say no to a day without offering another, you can ask one more time later. If they say no again without suggesting a new day, the next invitation should come from them.

sections.h: Make it clear it is a date
body: In many cultures, two people meeting for coffee could be friends or a date. If you want it to be a date, say so, kindly. Words like "date", "take you out" or "just the two of us" help. This is fairer to the other person, because they can answer the real question, and it saves you from weeks of not knowing.
If you are very nervous about the word "date", you can say: "I like you and I'd like to spend some time with you, just us." That is clear without being heavy.

ul: Asking in a way that makes no hard to say: in front of friends, with a big gift, or with a crowd watching.
Asking several times after a clear no.
Making them plan everything: "What do you want to do?" is harder to answer than a concrete idea.
Planning something very long, expensive or far away for a first date.
Asking through a friend, unless that is a normal custom where you live and you both know each other well.
Getting angry or cold if they say no. How you take a no shows who you are.

sections.h: Safety for first meetings with someone from an app
body: If you met online and have not met in person before, keep the first meeting safe for both of you. love is respect, a US nonprofit, recommends the first three steps below, and the US Federal Trade Commission warns about the last one. They apply everywhere:

ol: Meet in a busy public place, such as a cafe, not at either person's home.
Tell a friend where you are going, who you are meeting, and when you expect to be home.
Arrange your own transport there and back, so you choose when to leave and who knows your address.
A short video call before meeting helps you check that the person is real.
Never send money to someone you have not met. Requests for money, gift cards or crypto are a common sign of a romance scam.

body: Offering these yourself is also kind: "Let's meet at the cafe on Main Street. I'll come straight from work." It shows the other person you understand that meeting a stranger takes trust. For what to do on the day, see cv.cm's first date tips.

faq.q: Should I ask someone out over text or in person?
faq.a: Both work. In person can feel warmer; text gives them time to think and is common when you mostly talk online. Either way, be specific about the plan.

faq.q: What is a good first date to suggest?
faq.a: Something short, public and easy to talk during: coffee, a walk in a park, a dessert place, a small exhibition. Save films and loud places for later.

faq.q: How do I ask out a coworker without making things awkward?
faq.a: Ask once, privately and outside work tasks, say a no will not change anything, and keep that promise. Check whether your workplace has rules about this, especially if one of you manages the other.

faq.q: Who should pay when you ask someone out?
faq.a: Customs vary by country and couple. A common, simple approach is that the person who asked offers to pay, and you split it if the other person prefers.

faq.q: How many times can I ask someone out before giving up?
faq.a: After one no without a new day, you can ask one more time. After a second no, stop and let them make the next move.
